It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing a world where many seek to “remodel the way we think about truth” regarding the family, and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the biblical pattern of parenting and the discipline of the home in this hour? [13, 1341, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by a culture that offers “spiritual placebos” or suggests that children are mere “administrative anomalies” to be managed by human psychology, or are you seeking the “settled certainty” that the Master “sovereignly orders everything He has made”—including the raising of the next generation for His glory? [1, 13, 20, 1143, 1283, 1425, 1532, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many “shave off the edges” of the truth to avoid the “offense of the cross,” we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Lord personally governs the household by His perfect Law [11, 28, 68, 1503, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the parent’s role is not a “market-driven strategy” but a stewardship subject to the “binding and authoritative mandate” of the King of Kings [15, 68, 213, 1143, 1316, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The Blueprint of Diligent Discipleship**

**Verse**
“ ‘Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one! You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength. And these words which I command you today shall be in your heart. You shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, when you walk by the way, when you lie down, and when you rise up’ ” (Deuteronomy 6:4–7). [267, 733, 964, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Scripture reveals that the “sole objective” of the parent is to lead children to “fear the LORD” through a “right understanding of who He is,” and this instruction must be a “total way of life” rather than a “ritualized ceremony” [11, 14, 24, 101, 142, 965, 1503, Conversation History]. To “teach them diligently” means the Word of God must “dominate your attitudes and actions” so that your children see the “unvarnished truth” modeled in “unbroken conversation” [4, 11, 21, 116, 180, 1183, 1278, 1503, Conversation History]. The sources teach that “salvation is a supernatural work of God,” but parents are the chosen “instrumentality” by which children “learn to fear Me all the days they live on the earth” (Deuteronomy 4:10) [251, 262, 1130, 1503, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by the idea that “spiritual formation” is the church’s job alone, for “ ‘man shall not live by bread alone; but man lives by every word that proceeds from the mouth of the LORD’ ” (Deuteronomy 8:3) [10, 11, 562, 809, 811, 925, 1261, 1406, 1502, 1709, Conversation History]. Recognize that “your life is not your own,” and you must “discipline your mind” to “talk of them when you sit in your house,” for “the heart of the wise teaches his mouth” (Proverbs 16:23) [11, 12, 101, 113, 116, 562, 846, 1138, 1262, 1406, 1670, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **theocratic context**, the Shema was the “Keri’at Shema,” a daily public and private reading intended to preserve “national greatness” as a “temporal sign” of God’s favor (Deuteronomy 28:1) [409, 718, 1100, 1313, 1353, 1519, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this by showing that because “your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit,” the “truth which was once for all delivered” is now taught in the “assembly of the citizens of heaven,” where “true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth” (Jude 3; John 4:23; 1 Corinthians 6:19) [11, 12, 13, 21, 32, 92, 101, 186, 238, 240, 264, 402, 540, 571, 726, 792, 833, 837, 941, 963, 1036, 1054, 1059, 1093, 1117, 1118, 1119, 1120, 1138, 1202, 1208, 1219, 1220, 1243, 1262, 1267, 1276, 1313, 1315, 1316, 1402, 1403, 1406, 1417, 1426, 1431, 1491, 1503, 1515, 1636, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: The Heart of Loving Correction**

**Verse**
“He who spares his rod hates his son, but he who loves him disciplines him promptly” (Proverbs 13:24). [1105, Conversation History]. “Foolishness is bound up in the heart of a child; the rod of correction will drive it far from him” (Proverbs 22:15). [734, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed faith—echoed by **John MacArthur**—asserts that “children are a heritage from the LORD” who inherit a “fallen humanness,” and therefore “discipline is a way for God to display His grace and power” by “driving away” the “foolishness” of a “rebellious heart” [11, 15, 20, 268, 485, 713, 730, 774, 898, 1143, 1262, 1532, 1720, Conversation History]. Scripture handles the “noise and tumult” of parenting by revealing that “the testing of your faith produces patience,” and a parent’s “corrective priorities” must reflect the truth that “unbelief is the seed” of all disorder (James 1:3) [1, 11, 13, 31, 71, 125, 485, 733, 747, 886, 1012, 1132, 1313, 1388, 1408, 1503, 1515, Conversation History]. The “rod of correction” is not an instrument of “anger without cause,” but a “verbal cudgel” to “peel away the flesh and drive you to Himself,” for “judgment is God’s” (Matthew 5:22; Deuteronomy 1:17) [11, 15, 31, 37, 46, 63, 64, 79, 1132, 1143, 1235, 1321, 1332, 1343, 1406, 1408, 1473, 1503, 1515, 1709, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not look for some other fountain of knowledge” in “career” or “worldly success” for your child, but instead “train up a child in the way he should go” so they find “repose of the soul” in the “finished work” of Christ (Proverbs 22:6; John 19:30) [11, 24, 31, 51, 123, 142, 734, 1113, 1313, 1406, 1426, 1445, 1503, Conversation History]. Recognize that “he who trusts in his own heart is a fool,” and you must “discipline your body” to ensure your “holy motives result in holy behavior” in front of your little ones (Proverbs 28:26) [11, 12, 37, 79, 91, 101, 116, 172, 209, 251, 851, 1017, 1039, 1313, 1381, 1406, 1408, 1445, 1503, 1515, 1670, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Ritual vs. Reality**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “stubborn and rebellious sons” who were “gluttons and drunkards” were subject to “capital punishment” to “put away the evil from among you” (Deuteronomy 21:18, 20–21) [285, 700, 757, 1103, 1104, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “warfare,” teaching that while we “do not war according to the flesh,” we use the “sword of the Spirit” to “bring every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ,” replacing the physical sword with the “instruction in righteousness” (2 Corinthians 10:4–5; 2 Timothy 3:16) [11, 13, 21, 32, 43, 92, 113, 201, 211, 728, 750, 760, 805, 808, 922, 932, 1062, 1081, 1093, 1099, 1101, 1102, 1103, 1109, 1137, 1141, 1158, 1210, 1240, 1246, 1263, 1268, 1312, 1313, 1325, 1331, 1334, 1342, 1344, 1349, 1354, 1358, 1364, 1366, 1367, 1389, 1400, 1401, 1402, 1406, 1408, 1410, 1411, 1415, 1440, 1441, 1443, 1451, 1453, 1461, 1462, 1463, 1467, 1479, 1486, 1488, 1490, 1503, 1515, 1520, 1531, 1532, 1537, 1540, 1542, 1546, 1550, 1554, 1601, 1646, 1670, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: The Balance of Grace (Gospel Parenting)**

**Verse**
“And you, fathers, do not provoke your children to wrath, but bring them up in the training and admonition of the Lord” (Ephesians 6:4). [734, 1140, Conversation History]. “Fathers, do not provoke your children, lest they become discouraged” (Colossians 3:21). [469, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Paul Washer**—warns that “love is not defined by allowing those whom you love to have what they want,” yet “authoritarian harshness” is a “spirit of fraud” that “muffles the truth” [11, 1118, 1292, 1503, Conversation History]. To “provoke to wrath” occurs when a parent’s “heart is lifted up above his brethren,” forgetting that “your Master and theirs is in heaven,” and that “God shows no partiality” (Deuteronomy 17:20; Ephesians 6:9) [111, 152, 272, 542, 690, 703, 846, 858, 860, 1041, 1229, 1251, 1316, 1365, 1473, 1503, Conversation History]. The church militant is called to provide “instruction in the law” to give children a “right foundation” where “holy motives result in holy behavior” [11, 14, 37, 101, 965, 1118, 1406, 1503, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Trade in your worry for trust,” for your “Heavenly Father knows that you need all these things” and He “will never leave you nor forsake you” while you labor to “adorn the doctrine of God” in your home (Matthew 6:32; Hebrews 13:5; Titus 2:10) [11, 12, 38, 69, 86, 94, 201, 361, 407, 779, 799, 882, 1013, 1131, 1138, 1227, 1262, 1266, 1406, 1408, 1450, 1502, 1503, 1515, 1670, Conversation History]. You must “not look for some other fountain of knowledge” in “opinion polls” for parenting, but instead “ascribe greatness to our God” by recognize that “children are a reward” (Deuteronomy 32:3; Psalm 127:3) [51, 123, 125, 706, 730, 898, 905, 1406, 1503, 1623, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Roman context vs. Christian Vision**
Under **Roman Law**, the *patria potestas* gave a father “the right of life and death” over his children, treating them as “goods and chattels” [127, 129, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this by showing that “fathers shall not be put to death for their children... a person shall be put to death for his own sin,” and parents are merely “stewards” of children who belong to the “Heir of all things” (Deuteronomy 24:16; Hebrews 1:2) [290, 1113, 1313, 1315, 1503, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: The Peril of Permissive Neglect**

**Verse**
“ ‘Now Eli was very old; and he heard everything his sons did to all Israel... So he said to them, “Why do you do such things? For I hear of your evil dealings from all the people... If one man sins against another, God will judge him. But if a man sins against the LORD, who will intercede for him?” Nevertheless they did not heed the voice of their father’ ” (1 Samuel 2:22–25). [308, 772, Conversation History]. “ ‘He who justifies the wicked... Both of them alike are an abomination to the LORD’ ” (Proverbs 17:15). [170, 236, 1147, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The “record of history” reveals that Eli was a “derelict father” because he “neglected the weightier matters” of the Law and did not “restrain” his children from their “wicked deeds” [11, 15, 118, 130, 1143, 1248, 1255, 1316, 1365, 1422, 1532, 1720, Conversation History]. Permissive neglect is a “spirit of fraud” that “muffles the truth of God’s Word” with “trivial diversions,” acting as a “cradle of security” on the “precipice of hell” [1, 11, 28, 1503, Conversation History]. The Reformed tradition notes that “sin is the monarch that rules the heart,” and therefore a parent who “justify[ies] the wicked” acts as a “fowler’s snare” who “strengthen[s] the hands of evil doers” (Jeremiah 23:14) [11, 24, 72, 73, 170, 213, 236, 1131, 1136, 1147, 1264, 1266, 1323, 1365, 1384, 1406, 1483, 1503, 1512, 1515, 1516, 1605, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Wait for His Son from heaven,” knowing that “the Lord knows how to deliver the godly” and His “everlasting dominion” will judge every “unrighteous deception” in the home (1 Thessalonians 1:10; 2 Peter 2:9) [11, 14, 24, 47, 92, 94, 109, 121, 147, 176, 201, 352, 412, 602, 630, 852, 869, 948, 957, 1132, 1138, 1143, 1313, 1315, 1341, 1408, 1420, 1450, 1515, 1572, 1720, Conversation History]. You should find “tranquility of soul” by resting on the “surest foundation,” for “He who has begun a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ” (Philippians 1:6) [5, 11, 24, 25, 41, 47, 83, 92, 121, 147, 176, 198, 201, 211, 222, 273, 285, 292, 300, 313, 315, 324, 332, 352, 359, 361, 386, 405, 412, 413, 414, 442, 444, 449, 591, 602, 614, 630, 645, 646, 718, 719, 782, 788, 825, 829, 830, 836, 842, 844, 852, 856, 867, 869, 872, 881, 883, 913, 921, 934, 936, 940, 947, 957, 958, 975, 1012, 1016, 1032, 1033, 1035, 1113, 1132, 1138, 1143, 1181, 1183, 1214, 1221, 1225, 1300, 1301, 1306, 1311, 1312, 1313, 1315, 1406, 1407, 1408, 1420, 1426, 1440, 1441, 1445, 1447, 1450, 1502, 1503, 1515, 1532, 1572, 1614, 1646, 1670, 1684, 1720, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 87, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 291, 297, 300, 311, 324, 325, 332, 361, 405, 413, 414, 424, 444, 449, 591, 834, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

references.cited_text: Jesus reaffirmed to them what their Scripture taught and what faithful, godly Jews had always believed: God is the Father in heaven to those who trust in Him. In all His prayers, Jesus used the title Father, except when He was on the cross bearing the sin of the world and was forsaken by God (Matt. 27:46). Though the text of Matthew 6:9 uses the Greek word Pat∑r [ ], Jesus likely used the Aramaic word Abba since that is the language He and the majority of Palestinian Jews commonly spoke. Since Abba is equivalent to our term Daddy, Jesus would have used it to emphasize the personal and intimate relationship God has with His children.

Starting with that point, Jesus makes three practical exhortations regarding the believer’s attitude toward “unrighteous mammon”—money. He is outlining for His disciples how their perspective on money should shape their thoughts and behavior toward others, self, and God (in that order). Here are the key points of wisdom Jesus draws from His parable about the unjust steward. Lesson 1: Money is a resource to be used for the good of others. Immediately after commending the shrewdness of the sons of this world for their forward-thinking resourcefulness, Jesus adds this word of advice for His disciples: “And I say to you, make friends for yourselves by unrighteous mammon, that when [it fails], they may receive you into an everlasting home” (Luke 16:9). Use your money to make friends—not earthly friends, but friends who will welcome you into your eternal home. In other words, be generous with the people of God. Put your money to work for others; help the truly needy among God’s people; “and you will have treasure in heaven” (Matt. 19:21). Remember the words of Jesus in Matthew 25:35–40: “I was hungry and you gave Me food; I was thirsty and you gave Me drink; I was a stranger and you took Me in; I was naked and you clothed Me; I was sick and you visited Me; I was in prison and you came to Me… . Inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these My brethren, you did it to Me” (emphasis added).
